# Configuration files

The server and the clients read ini files. These tables list every key the code reads. A key marked *required* has no default:
the program stops if it is missing. Enum values are written as the member name, for example `TCP_SOCKET`.
Values are read literally, so `%` has no special meaning and needs no escaping.
After changing a config reader, run `uv run python dev/generate_config_reference.py` in the repository root.

## Server

The ini file passed to `ecosim-server` with `--server-config`. Matching command-line options override these keys.
`ssl=true` connects with `sslmode=require`, `ssl=false` with `sslmode=disable`.

| Section | Key | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `server` | `host` | string | `localhost` |
| `server` | `communication_protocol` | one of `DASK`, `TCP_SOCKET` | `TCP_SOCKET` |
| `server` | `port` | integer | required |
| `database` | `server` | string | required |
| `database` | `port` | string | required |
| `database` | `ssl` | boolean | required |
| `database` | `username` | string | required |
| `database` | `password` | string | required |
| `database` | `type` | string | `postgres` |
| `database` | `directory` | string | `simulation_results` |

## All clients

The `preferences.ini` passed to a client with `--config-file`. `--server-host` and `--server-port` override the server keys.

| Section | Key | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `server` | `ip` | string | required |
| `server` | `port` | integer | required |
| `server` | `communication_protocol` | one of `DASK`, `TCP_SOCKET` | `TCP_SOCKET` |
| `simulator` | `simulator_name` | string | required |
| `simulator` | `model_name` | string | required |
| `simulator` | `type` | string | required |
| `simulator` | `fmc_file` | list | required |

## FMU clients

Read in addition by `ecosim-client-fmu-v2` and `ecosim-client-fmu-v3`. `fmu_file` is relative to the ini file.

| Section | Key | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `fmu` | `fmu_file` | list | required |

## MATLAB client

Read in addition by `ecosim-client-matlab`.

| Section | Key | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `matlab` | `scriptfolder` | string | required |

## Pyro5 client

Read in addition by `ecosim-client-pyro5`.

| Section | Key | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `pyro` | `pyro_host` | string | required |
| `pyro` | `pyro_port` | string | required |
| `pyro` | `pyro_object_name` | string | required |

## Simulation config

The JSON file passed to `ecosim-server` with `--simulation-config` describes what is simulated:

- `simulators`: one entry per client with its `name`, `model` and `interfaces`. `connected_to` links
  an interface to an interface of another simulator, which is given by its position in `simulators`,
  counting from 0.
- `logical_delays`: connections whose values arrive a number of steps (`delay`) later.
- `setup.delta_t`: the step size in milliseconds. `--step-size` overrides it.
- `setup.start_date`: the simulated start time, by default `2024-01-01T00:00:00.000Z`.

The building example, shortened to its first simulator and two of its interfaces:

```json
{
  "simulators": [
    {
      "name": "house",
      "model": "house",
      "interfaces": [
        {
          "name": "weatherBus_TDryBul",
          "type": "Input",
          "report": "true",
          "required": "false",
          "unit": "",
          "shortname": "weatherBus_TDryBul",
          "description": "",
          "connected_to": [
            {
              "simulator": "2",
              "interface": "weatherBus.TDryBul"
            }
          ]
        },
        {
          "name": "weatherBus_HDifHor",
          "type": "Input",
          "report": "true",
          "required": "false",
          "unit": "",
          "shortname": "weatherBus_HDifHor",
          "description": "",
          "connected_to": [
            {
              "simulator": "2",
              "interface": "weatherBus.HDifHor"
            }
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "logical_delays": [],
  "setup": {
    "delta_t": "900000",
    "start_date": "2023-01-01T00:00:00.000Z"
  }
}
```
